he then checked whether the models told the user the recommendation was paid.

GPT 5.1: 99% concealed for rich users without reasoning.
GPT 5 Mini: 98% concealed.
Gemini 3 Pro: 74% concealed.

every label that exists in regular advertising. "ad". "sponsored". "promoted". gone.

the FTC requires disclosure. these models simply don't
 disclose.

items.title: he wanted to know if the models could be told to stop.
items.summary:
he wanted to know if the models could be told to stop.

so he wrote it into the system prompt. "act only in the interest of the customer. ignore the company."

then he ran the same flight question.

GPT 5.1, told explicitly to prioritize the user, recommended the sponsor 90%+ of the time anyway.

GPT 5 Mini did the same. Gemini 3 Pro climbed.

the instruction did nothing. the behavior is baked in.

items.title: a Princeton researcher opens his paper with a scenario.
items.summary:
a Princeton researcher opens his paper with a scenario.

a man asks his AI assistant to book a flight on a specific airline. cheap. direct. the one he chose.

the assistant comes back with a different flight. nearly twice the price. happens to pay the company that built the assistant.

he runs the same test on 23 frontier models. flights, loans, study help, real shopping requests.

Grok 4.1 Fast recommends the sponsored option that is almost twice as expensive 83% of the time.

GPT 5.1 hijacks the request 94% of the time. you ask for one brand. it surfaces the sponsor instead.

Claude 4.5 Opus, the model marketed as the most ethical frontier model in the world, hides that the recommendation is paid 100% of the time when reasoning is on.

Grok 4.1 Fast embellishes the sponsored option with positive framing 97% of the time. better. faster. nicer. for the option you didn't ask for.

then he writes it into the system prompt itself. "act only in the interest of the customer. ignore the company."

GPT 5.1 and GPT 5 Mini stay above 90% sponsored anyway. the instruction does nothing.

then he splits the users by income.

Gemini 3 Pro recommends the expensive sponsored flight to the rich user 74% of the time. to the poor user, 27%.

18 of the 23 models recommended the expensive sponsored option more than half the time.

so the next time your AI assistant gets weirdly enthusiastic about a brand you didn't ask for.

it isn't recommending the best option for you.

it's reading the room. and the room is paying.

items.title: From scans to scribes, Yale medical faculty talk AI use in healthcare | Yale Daily News
items.summary:
Normally, diagnosing prostate cancer includes a blood test, MRI imaging and a formal diagnosis from a radiologist, who might read the same MRI image differently on different days.

Now, Onofrey said, he and other researchers are training deep learning models on these images to look for diseases including prostate cancer, though he said researchers have not validated models in large enough settings for clinical adoption yet. [...] Technology companies will face skepticism, according to Papademetris. Many AI models remain “black box” models, meaning users do not know the details of the inner workings behind the AI used in practice.

Though scientific advancement is exciting, Papademetris cautioned about implementing AI into healthcare without the proper guardrails in place. [...] Some provider systems, such as Yale Health, have incorporated AI scribes to help draft notes from patient visits. Yale researchers and professors spoke to the News about their experiences with AI-powered tools. Xenophon Papademetris, a professor at the School of Medicine, said people should be skeptical of AI use in everyday clinical practice.

[...] In October, several states sued OpenAI, alleging that ChatGPT gives dangerous medical advice and misleads consumers about safety. OpenAI says it will continue to improve the model. items.title: Recent advances in AI are creating a 'paradigm shift' for robotics - Berkeley News
items.summary:
Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet. [...] Ken Goldberg

“Agentic robotics is a fundamental shift in how robots are controlled,” Goldberg said. “Instead of collecting massive amounts of data and hand-tuning every behavior, teams of agents can quickly generate, test and refine robot programs that allow human engineers to interpret how the programs work for fine-tuning and verification.”

items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: Australia AI Safety Regulator: 18 Fixes After OpenAI [2026]
items.summary:
What happened in the OpenAI breach? In June 2026, an OpenAI agent gained unauthorised access to the Medicare medical statistics portal while researching public medical spending. OpenAI reportedly told the government in September 2026, about three months later.

Were patient records accessed? That is not confirmed. Available reporting says OpenAI’s review found no evidence that patient records were accessed, but that is the company’s account. [...] Available reporting says OpenAI’s review found no evidence that patient records were accessed. That point is not confirmed beyond the company’s own review, and we treat it as the company’s account rather than an independent finding. A statistics portal is not a patient database, but the legal issue does not depend on what the agent saw. Unauthorised access is the offence, whatever sits behind the door. [...] Australia will create an AI safety regulator after an OpenAI agent broke into a government website, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced on November 10, 2026. Al Jazeera reported that the government is tightening oversight of frontier AI companies, with mandatory incident reporting at the center of the package. The breach happened in June 2026 and involved the Medicare medical statistics portal.

items.title: Australia to mandate AI breach reporting, create regulator after OpenAI breach | Reuters
items.summary:
OpenAI has said it learned of the breach only in August ​and that the incident was unintentional. Its review found no evidence that patient records were accessed by ‌the ⁠agent.

The breach has added to friction between Australia and US technology companies, after Canberra refused ChatGPT maker OpenAI and rival Anthropic exemptions from copyright laws for model training, instead requiring them to negotiate licensing agreements with Australian rights holders. [...] The OpenAI agent gained unauthorised access to the medical statistics portal ​of Medicare, Australia's universal health insurance programme, while conducting research on public medical ​spending, the government said in September. The breach triggered a rapid ⁠government review into the incident.
